newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures trade slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures trade slightly higher.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures traded slightly higher, as the U.S. October Producer Price Index (PPI) data marginally cut into opening gains in yen, marks and Swiss francs, traders and analysts said.
U.S. PPI rose 0.4 percent, versus the average trade estimate of up 0.2 percent, for its biggest gain since March 1996 when the index rose 0.5 percent.
However, the stronger-than-expected growth in the overall index was overshadowed by the 0.3-percent decline in the core rate, excluding food and energy prices.
The data did little to spark a rally or sell-off in the U.S. dollar, and kept December yen, marks and Swiss francs locked inside of Tuesday's ranges.

December marks rose to $0.6656 as Bundesbank officials continued to jawbone the U.S. dollar higher. In a magazine interview, Bundesbank council member Olaf Sievert said there was no scope at present for a cut in German interest rates.
The market latched onto his comment as the latest in German support for a higher U.S. dollar.
However, the dollar remained under Tuesday's high of 1.5096, or $0.6638 December, and trades in a five-month range.
Sievert also said that the central bank was still open as to how the monetary policy situation would look after a couple of months.

Sterling's gains were more decisive at the opening after the British unemployment rate fell to a five-and-a-half-year low of 7.2 percent in October. The U.K. employment minister, Eric Forth, also said the Office of National Statistics was looking for a decline of 15,000 to 20,000 per month.
"We're on trend for that," he said.
The decline suggested the Bank of England may be more likely to raise interest rates.

In addition, Bank of England (BOE) governor Eddie George advised Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke at the September 23 monetary meeting to raise interest rates by a quarter-point to six percent. George also warned that interest rates might have to rise even further.
December sterling rose to $1.6534, near the contract high of $1.6560.
December yen briefly dipped lower, and is forecast to continue its descent in the near term, several floor traders said. The contract held above the $0.009000 level, or about 111.50 spot yen.

At 0808 CST/1408 GMT, December yen were off $0.000001 at $0.009005, marks were up $0.0015 at $0.6658, Swiss francs were $0.0014 higher at $0.7923, sterling was $0.0076 higher at $1.6524, Canadian dollars were $0.0010 lower at $0.7511, Australian dollars were $0.0005 higher at $0.7872 and Mexican pesos were $0.000125 lower at $0.123200. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
